title: Company-wide policies and process documentation: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees and managers to ensure consistent, auditable, and compliant operations.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors, and consultants who interact with corporate systems, cloud infrastructure, data stores, vendors, procurement processes, and travel/expense programs. Areas with additional regulatory or contractual controls (e.g., private customer deployments, regulated customer data, or classified vendor relationships) remain subject to supplementary controls documented under security-and-compliance.

1) Roles and ownership

- People Ops: policy maintenance, training, travel & expense program administration.
- Security & Compliance: access policy design, RBAC enforcement, vendor security reviews, data classification.
- Finance & Legal: procurement approvals, vendor contracting, expense policy enforcement, audits.
- Managers (all teams): day-to-day approvals for access, purchases within delegated budgets, travel pre-approvals.
- Engineering SRE & Platform: operational change coordination, maintenance windows, runbooks.

Each policy section below includes an assigned owner for operational questions.

2) Access & permissions (Owner: security-and-compliance)

Purpose: Ensure employees and contractors have the minimum privileges necessary to perform their roles while enabling timely onboarding and offboarding.

Key controls:
- Principle of least privilege: roles and groups are defined centrally; individual direct grants are discouraged.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): Azure/AWS/GCP IAM or internal systems map to corporate roles (e.g., engineering-readonly, infra-admin, product-analytics).
- Access request process:
  1. Employee/manager initiates request via the Access Request form (link in Templates section).
  2. Manager approves and documents business justification.
  3. Security reviews requests that grant privileged roles (admin, production access) within 48 hours.
  4. Provisioning is completed by the system owner or IAM automation team and logged.
- Temporary elevated access: granted via Just-in-Time (JIT) flow for up to 8 hours, requires pre-approval and audit logging.
- Offboarding: managers must submit Revocation request on the employee termination date (HR triggers automated deprovisioning for central SaaS).
- Access reviews: quarterly access certification run by managers; security will escalate stale approvals older than 90 days.
- MFA: required for all corporate accounts with access to code, production, or sensitive data.

3) Change management (Owner: eng-platform + eng-sre)

Purpose: Minimize unplanned outages and ensure traceable, reversible changes to production and critical systems.

Change classes:
- Standard (pre-approved routine ops) – low risk (e.g., scheduled config refresh) – no CAB required.
- Normal (planned changes) – requires Change Request (CR) at least 72 hours before deployment and CAB review for medium/high impact.
- Emergency – unplanned, immediate remediation; must be declared via the Emergency Change workflow, implemented with the smallest blast radius, and followed by a post-change review within 48 hours.

Change process (normal changes):
 1. Raise CR in Change Tracker (template in Templates). Include owner, rollback plan, testing plan, and SLO impact.
 2. Assign risk level and required approvers.
 3. CAB meets weekly; high-risk changes require demonstration in staging.
 4. Schedule within maintenance windows: default Tues 02:00–04:00 UTC (low traffic).
 5. Execute change, monitor for 1.5x expected recovery window; if anomalous, trigger rollback.
 6. Complete post-change report within 3 business days.

Operational thresholds:
- Changes affecting customer-facing SLAs require business and legal sign-off.
- Rollback target: within 30 minutes for critical failures.

4) Data management (Owner: security-and-compliance + eng-data)

Data classification:
- Public: safe to publish.
- Internal: company-internal use only.
- Confidential: customer data, PII, or regulated information.
- Restricted: highest sensitivity (legal, contracts, security keys).

Handling rules:
- Confidential/Restricted data must be stored in approved encrypted stores (KMS-backed).
- Access to Confidential/Restricted data requires explicit approval and logging; all uses audited.
- Data retention: default retention is 18 months for internal logs, 7 years for financial records, and per-contract retention for customer data (see related customer contracts).
- Backups: daily incremental, weekly full backups; automated restore tests quarterly.
- Data disposal: documented deletion requests routed through Data Governance; data destruction confirmed in writing.

Data incident response:
- Any suspected data exposure must be reported to security-and-compliance within 2 hours.
- Incident playbook: initial triage, containment, customer notification (as required), remediation, and regulatory reporting handled by security & legal.

5) Procurement & expenses (Owner: finance-and-legal)

Procurement approval matrix (effective):
| Amount | Approver | Notes |
| <$5,000 | Hiring manager | May be auto-approved for pre-approved vendors |
| $5,000–$50,000 | Finance Manager | Requires PO; finance validates budget |
| >$50,000 | VP-level + Legal review | Requires contract and vendor security review |

Process highlights:
- All purchases of software and cloud services require a vendor risk intake (security questionnaire) before purchase where the vendor will access sensitive data or systems.
- Use corporate POs for purchases over $5k; do not accept auto-renewing vendor terms without Legal review for contracts >$50k.
- Expense reimbursements must be submitted within 30 days with receipts via the Expense System. Corporate card holders must reconcile monthly.
- Travel pre-approval: domestic travel requires manager sign-off; international travel requires People Ops approval for visas, insurance and higher per-diem allowances.

6) Vendor management (Owner: finance-and-legal + security-and-compliance)

Onboarding checklist:
- Business justification and owner assigned.
- Vendor risk questionnaire completed and reviewed by Security.
- Standard contract (NDAs, DPA) approved by Legal.
- Procurement PO or contract executed.
- Vendor access limited to least privilege and timebound.

Vendor review cadence:
- High-risk vendors: annual security review and quarterly operational check-ins.
- Low-risk vendors: review every 24 months.

Termination:
- Offboarding includes account termination, key rotation, retrieval/destruction of corporate data, and confirmation of license/cost stop.

7) Travel policy (Owner: people-ops + finance-and-legal)

Booking & approvals:
- Employees must use company travel portal for flights and hotels.
- Manager pre-approval required. International travel requires People Ops notification for mandatory travel safety check.

Allowances and limits:
- Economy standard for flights under 6 hours; premium economy allowed for 6+ hour flights with Manager approval.
- Hotel: business-class hotels; use corporate rate where available.
- Per diem: $75 domestic, $150 international (custom allowances available for high-cost cities as listed in the travel template).

Expense filing:
- Submit itemized receipts within 14 days of trip end.
- Non-compliant expenses (alcohol > policy limits, personal charges) may be reduced from reimbursement.

Emergency travel:
- For urgent travel, employees may book directly but must submit justification and receipts; People Ops will retroactively approve if within policy.

8) Internal templates and links (Owner: people-ops)

Templates (available in the Templates library):
- Access Request Form (access-request-template.docx)
- Change Request and Rollback Plan (change-request-template.md)
- Vendor Security Questionnaire (vendor-security-questionnaire.pdf)
- Purchase Order & Procurement Request (po-request-form.xlsx)
- Travel Pre-Approval & Expense Report (travel-expense-template.xlsx)

How to use templates:
1. Copy the appropriate template into your team namespace.
2. Fill required fields (owner, cost center, business justification, risk assessment).
3. Submit according to the process described in each policy section.

9) Audit, compliance, and continuous improvement

- Policies reviewed annually by People Ops, Finance, and Security. Significant changes require cross-functional review and executive approval.
- Regular audits: security conducts quarterly access audits; finance runs procurement audit semi-annually.
- Exceptions: documented exception requests must include compensating controls, a defined time window, and approval from owner team and security.

Appendices

A. Contacts and escalation paths:
- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security & Compliance: security@redwood.ai
- Finance & Legal: finance-legal@redwood.ai
- IT & IAM automation: infra-iam@redwood.ai

B. Quick checklists:
- New hire: submit Access Request, assign manager approver, schedule onboarding access review at day 30.
- New vendor: complete Vendor Questionnaire, Legal review, PO/contract before prod access.

C. Version history:
- 2026-03-21: Initial consolidated published policy (A. Martinez).
- 2026-03-22: Minor edits: clarified procurement thresholds and travel per-diem rates (reviewers: E. Chen, P. Kapoor).

End of document.
